episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.

transcript_window.text: My heart and my spirit tells me that I'm here to help educate young people, hold them accountable.
And if that means, you know, they miss a game here because they have to be held accountable, then, then so be it.
But that's getting harder and harder to do in a world of social media and instant feedback and, and instant gratification.
And so there, there is this tug of war going on between how do we get back to a center where we're kind of in the business of educating young people again.
Yeah, I lean into that transformational approach, and it's hard to execute this day and age because of all the distractive nature that are pulling all these different ways.
And I think it speaks to human nature, too, when you're talking about, you know, you're really good at your job.
There's a certain advocacy for self and preservation, Preservation and as well as just human nature is to do what's best for yourself and whatever entity that you're representing at the time to win.
And winning is why we compete too.
We want to compete and win, but it is a balance or it's a nuanced thing that it's hard to find balance in.
So best paths forward, there's headwinds.
There are opportunities here to resolve and solve.
If you're sequencing, right, if you're trying to address biggest problems first, like I was talking to Graham Rossini, for instance, he's like, we've got to figure out agents.
We've got too many bad players.
We need some sort of an accreditation.
That's where he's leaning right now from a problem -solve standpoint.
Where are you leaning right now?
What problems do you want to solve kind of first things first?
Well, I think the limited antitrust protection, right?
I mean, it's just not conducive to parity if Louisiana has a different set of rules for their NIL and revenue share than Florida does.
And so, you know, we are such a keep up with the Joneses.
Our world is if I'll follow that rule as long as all my opponents are going to follow that rule.
But the minute there's that creep of, well, if Notre Dame gets to do it, then we're going to do it.
And that's, again, it goes back to people want to keep their jobs.
People want to win.
an advantage.
And so I think that that antitrust is really important.
